title: Reconciliation workflow between paper registers and the app
description: Wardens keep decades of history on paper and are only entering new activity into the app going forward - they are not confident the two records will stay in sync, and have no way to mark 'this paper entry is now also in the app' or spot gaps. Needs a lightweight way to track reconciliation status rather than forcing a full migration (see LODGY-44).
acceptanceCriteria: Warden can mark a period (e.g. a given month for a given hostel) as 'reconciled with paper records'
Reconciled periods are visually distinguished from not-yet-reconciled ones in the Monthly Report / Payments views
This is a manual attestation, not an automated diff against anything - it does not block or alter any data

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.
Starting - a per-hostel, per-month reconciliation attestation stored in its own table (DB v3), shown on the Monthly Report and nowhere allowed to alter or gate data.

Reconciliation is a per-hostel, per-month attestation and nothing more. New ReconciliationMark entity (hostelId + periodMonth + periodYear, unique index on that triple so a period cannot be marked twice, CASCADE on hostel delete, optional note field reserved for later) with its own DAO and ReconciliationRepository; DB to version 3 with MIGRATION_2_3, again diffed against Room's exported schemas/3.json and matching it exactly. Surfaced on the Monthly Report as a 'Checked against paper records' switch, reading either 'You marked this month as matching your register' or 'Not checked against your register yet', and carried into the CSV export so a saved or printed report says whether it was reconciled. AC 3 is the important one and holds by construction: the mark lives in its own table, is written and read only by this switch, and no query anywhere filters, alters or gates on it - nothing is diffed against anything, and turning the switch back off deletes the row, so a mistaken attestation is reversible. MonthlyReportViewModelTest covers reading an existing mark, and that toggling writes then removes it. testDebugUnitTest green.

FAIL on AC2 - only half the requirement is built. AC1 passes: the Monthly Report has a 'Checked against paper records' switch that marks a given month for a given hostel, the state persists (re-opened 9/2026 later and it still read 'You marked this month as matching your register'), and it is stored as its own reconciliation_marks row. AC3 passes: it is purely a manual attestation - flipping it altered no invoice, payment or total, and nothing is diffed or blocked. AC2 says 'Reconciled periods are visually distinguished from not-yet-reconciled ones in the Monthly Report / Payments views'. The Monthly Report does this (the switch plus 'You marked this month as matching your register.' vs 'Not checked against your register yet.'), and the CSV export carries it too. The Payments view does not. WHAT I DID: marked 8/2026 as reconciled, then opened the Invoices list. WHAT I EXPECTED: the 8/2026 invoice visually distinguished from the unreconciled 6/2026 and 7/2026 ones. WHAT HAPPENED: all three rows render identically - no badge, tint or marker of any kind. Confirmed in code: grepping for 'reconcil' across ui/ returns hits only in MonthlyReportScreen/ViewModel; nothing in the invoice list or its ViewModel consumes ReconciliationRepository. SUGGESTED FIX: surface the period's reconciled state on the invoice row (a small 'checked' marker keyed on the invoice's periodMonth/periodYear plus hostel). PO NOTE: if 'Monthly Report / Payments views' was only ever meant to mean the report screen, say so and I will pass this on the next round - I am reading the slash as naming two screens.

Fixed - reconciliation state now appears on the Payments view as well as the Monthly Report. InvoiceListItem gains `periodReconciled`; the ViewModel combines the invoices flow with a new ReconciliationRepository.observeAll() and matches each invoice on (hostelId, periodMonth, periodYear). The hostel is resolved per invoice via a new BedDao.getHostelId(bedId) join (beds -> rooms -> floors), because the invoice list spans every hostel rather than a selected one - matching on period alone would have wrongly marked another hostel's invoices. The row renders a check icon plus the text 'Checked against register' in the LODGY-36 GOOD token, so it follows LODGY-62's icon-plus-label rule rather than colour alone. New strings reconciliation_badge in values/ and values-hi/. Because it is driven by an observed query, toggling the switch on the Monthly Report updates the invoice list without a restart. VERIFIED ON EMULATOR: 8/2026, the period QA marked reconciled this morning, now shows the badge while 6/2026 and 7/2026 do not. Build and full suite green: 412 tests pass (4 new), ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest and assembleDebug both successful. Tests touched for the new signatures: TenantProfileViewModelTest and TenantDirectoryViewModelTest now mock the observed agreement flows, InvoiceListViewModelTest gains the ReconciliationRepository mock, and DataPacketTest gains the noticeGiven label. Note on two profile tests: they assert state after setPlannedMoveOut, which previously passed only because the ViewModel wrote the value optimistically. Rather than keep that second source of truth - the exact bug class LODGY-33 is about - the mocks now use a MutableStateFlow that re-emits on write, which is how Room actually behaves.

PASS - and I specifically tried to break the new hostel-matching logic, because keying a badge on period alone would have been an easy and invisible bug. AC1 and AC3 were already passing and still are. AC2 is now met on BOTH surfaces the criterion names. The test that matters: I built a second hostel (Moonlight, Room 501, tenant Priya) and gave it an invoice for 8/2026 - the SAME period already marked reconciled on Sunrise PG. Filtered the invoice list to month 8 so both sat side by side: Sunrise's 8/2026 row carried 'Checked against register' and Moonlight's 8/2026 row did NOT. So the badge follows the hostel, not just the period - a period-only match would have wrongly flagged Priya's invoice. Then I marked Moonlight's 8/2026 reconciled on its own Monthly Report and returned to the invoice list WITHOUT restarting: Priya's row picked up the badge immediately, confirming it is driven by an observed query rather than a one-shot read. The badge pairs a check icon with the text 'Checked against register' in the LODGY-36 GOOD token, so it satisfies LODGY-62's icon-plus-label rule rather than relying on colour alone, and it is translated in values-hi.
